name: Rinn
kurzbeschreibung: Highest village in the municipality of Rinn, featuring an impressive pilgrimage church with sweeping views over the entire Inntal.
beschreibung:
Überblick

Rinn is situated in the Innsbruck-Land district on a sun-drenched plateau of the southeastern low mountain terrace at an elevation of 918 metres, home to around 1,940 residents. Located merely ten kilometres east of Tyrol's provincial capital Innsbruck, the village nestles at the foot of Mount Glungezer (2,677 m). Surrounded by alpine meadows, larch groves, and pine forests, Rinn provides sweeping panoramic vistas across the Inn Valley and the rugged peaks of the Nordkette in the Karwendel mountains. The village preserves its traditional rural atmosphere with historic farmsteads, attracting sports enthusiasts with its championship golf course, toboggan trails, and scenic walking routes.

Geschichte

Rinn was first documented in 1250 under the name Runne, signifying forest clearance or a mountain water channel. The parish church dedicated to Saint Andrew originated from a 1481 Gothic building. In 1775 and 1776, master builder Franz Singer rebuilt the church in cheerful Rococo style, strongly influenced by the architectural vision of Tyrolean priest-architect Franz de Paula Penz. The ceiling frescoes were executed by Franz and Josef Giner, with altarpieces associated with Josef Schöpf. In the hamlet of Judenstein stands the Church of the Visitation, consecrated in 1678. Rinn is historically linked to Tyrolean freedom fighter Josef Speckbacher, who farmed here and became renowned as the Man of Rinn in 1809.

Anreise

Reaching Rinn is easy and swift. Motorists travel from the Inntalautobahn A12 via the Innsbruck-Ost exit through Aldrans or the Hall-Mitte exit through Tulfes along the L9 state road, arriving in 10 to 15 minutes. Train passengers arrive at Innsbruck main railway station or Hall in Tirol. From Innsbruck main station, VVT regional bus line 540 operates every half hour directly to Rinn village square and onward to Hall in Tirol. A weekend night bus ensures smooth evening connections.

Tipps

Golf aficionados praise the 18-hole championship course of Golfclub Innsbruck-Igls in Rinn, featuring alpine elevation shifts, mountain panoramas, and the signature island green on hole 12. During winter, the 3.8-kilometre natural toboggan track descending from the Rinner Alm mountain hut (1,394 m) offers thrilling runs with a separate ascent path and illuminated night sledding. Hikers appreciate the historical Speckbacher heritage trail and direct connections to the panoramic Zirbenweg trail on Mount Glungezer. A cultural tour of Saint Andrew's Rococo church and the memorial site in Judenstein completes the visit.
